report.headline: Usage projected to jump to 25.9% in the EuroLeague, well above league average, but the shooting-efficiency projection is unreliable and both estimates carry wide bands.

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 25.9% in the EuroLeague, up from 21.2% in the 2007-08 NBA season (+0.23 sd), placing the projection roughly 1.2 EuroLeague standard deviations above the league's mean usage of 20.6% (sd 4.4%).

risks.text: The true shooting percentage projection (57.7%) should not be trusted: the model's out-of-fold error (4.5%) is worse than simply predicting the EuroLeague average (4.3%).
Even the trustworthy usage projection carries a wide interval: the 80% band (21.5%-30.2%) spans about two EuroLeague standard deviations (sd 4.4%), and the 95% band (19.2%-32.5%) is wider still.

Players who historically made this NBA-to-EuroLeague move sat on average 0.31 sd below their own league's mean, a different profile from this subject's own +0.23 sd usage standing, which adds uncertainty about how representative the cohort is.

Simple alternative estimates disagree sharply: a naive 0.75x scaling of source usage gives 15.9%, versus the model's 25.9% and an exact-standing baseline of 21.6%, showing real sensitivity to method choice.

strengths.text: The usage projection sits well above the EuroLeague average — 25.9% against a league mean of 20.6% (sd 4.4%) — and the model beats a trivial baseline on this metric (3.2% MAE vs 4.2%).
The subject already carried an above-average usage share in the NBA (21.2%, +0.23 sd) across a full 82-game, 2,117-minute season, indicating an established high-usage role.
The fitted slope for usage carryover on this transition path is 0.977, meaning nearly all of a player's standing above their league is expected to transfer to the EuroLeague.
The usage estimate rests on a substantial historical base of 115 NBA-to-EuroLeague transitions.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 21.5% to 30.2% and the 95% interval from 19.2% to 32.5% — a span of roughly two EuroLeague standard deviations (sd 4.4%), meaning the model can rank the subject relative to peers but cannot pin a single number. The true shooting projection of 57.7% cannot be trusted at all: the model's out-of-fold error on that metric (4.5%) is worse than simply predicting the EuroLeague average (4.3%).
